name: A Holonomy Shore Has a Contracted Split-Square Marker
statement: Let $K\subsetneq A$ be dismantlable ample, put $D=A\setminus K$, suppose no concept of $D$ can be adjoined amply to $K$, and assume $|D|\le11$. If coordinate $z$ is constant on $D$ and its shore $S_z=\{d\in D:d^{\oplus z}\in K\}$ satisfies $2\le|S_z|<|D|$, then after contracting $z$ some image of $u\in D\setminus S_z$ can be adjoined amply to $\pi_zK$. It cannot lift to $K$; consequently an active edge $uu^{\oplus f}$ crosses into $S_z$ and its opposite square is split, with $(u^{\oplus f})^{\oplus z}\in K$ but $u^{\oplus z}\notin A$.
proof: Projection identifies the relative concepts of $\pi_zK\subsetneq\pi_zA$ with the distinct images of $D\setminus S_z$, whose number lies between one and nine. Both projected endpoints are dismantlable ample, so the sub-ten first-concept lemma supplies an addable projected root $u$. Its lift is blocked in $K$. The wrong-side witness theorem applies because the other member of its $z$-fibre lies neither in $D$, where $z$ is constant, nor in $K$. It yields a direction $f$ with $u^{\oplus f}\in D$ and $u^{\oplus\{z,f\}}\in K$, which is exactly the crossing edge and split square.
